newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian minister hopes for Russia flight deal.
newsitem.headline: Latvian minister hopes for Russia flight deal.

text.p: Latvian Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans will visit Moscow to ask permission for Latvia's national airline to fly to Russia, officials said on Monday.
Krishtopans visits Moscow from December 4 to 6 to negotiate a deal that will allow Air Baltic, part-owned by Scandinavian Airlines, to fly to Moscow and St Petersburg.
Moscow has so far refused to give Air Baltic slots because of debts owed by former Latvian airline, Latavio.
"Krishtopans is going to talk about Air Baltic flights to Russia," transport ministry aviation department head Arnis Muizhnieks told Reuters.
Latvia argues that two Russian airlines -- Transaero and Aeroflot -- are flying to Latvia and only one Latvian airline, Riair, flies to Moscow.
Muizhnieks said Latvia was ready to repay the debts but still considered this a separate issue from the number of flights.
"The Latvian side recognises, as it always has, that the debts have to be repaid in one way or another," he said.
Latvia recently refused to confirm Aeroflot's winter schedule to Riga, meaning that the Russian airline had to suspend its flights.
But the Latvian side reversed the decision and Aeroflot resumed flights around one week ago.
